target_customer: Companies that relocate or hire internationally, and the employees who move
problem: Cross-border relocation involves visas, immigration paperwork and settling in, handled by slow agencies and lawyers. Employers wanted one platform for it.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus services (immigration and relocation services per employee move)

founders.name: Hanna Marie Asmussen
founders.background_notes: Per Startup City Hamburg story: associate at BCG from 2016.

founders.name: Lisa Dahlke
founders.background_notes: HR expert, handled onboarding at Goodgame Studios per Startup City Hamburg.

founders.name: Franziska Löw
founders.background_notes: Described as bringing software programming knowledge.

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow software for immigration cases and relocation tasks, combined with in-house service teams. Mostly standard web engineering; the difficulty was operational and legal.

defensibility.rationale: Service delivery and country coverage took time to build, but competing agencies and software firms could copy the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent agencies stayed in the market; consolidation came later, with Deel buying LegalPad in 2022 and Boundless buying Localyze in 2025.

market_need_then: Companies hiring across borders needed visa and relocation support; the founders began from personal experience of moving abroad and found employers to be the stronger buyer.

branding.name_origin: Idea pitched as Localize at a Hamburg event in November 2016; the y spelling was adopted in 2017 to obtain a German domain. Meaning beyond that not stated.
branding.domain_note: Spelling changed from Localize to Localyze in 2017 to get localyze.de per Startup City Hamburg.

identity.visual_style: Moved from tech-heavy B2B SaaS look to softer, human-centric visuals with people photography
identity.voice_and_tone: Human, open, borderless; slogan about freeing talent from borders

rebrands.why: To speak to both company and employee customers, per the company blog
Smoother, softer, human-centric look, per company blog

brand_strength.rationale: Company publishes brand guidelines and rebranded twice, but no evidence of external buzz or brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Platform for employees settling into a new country
pivots.why: Team found employers to be the stronger market, per Startup City Hamburg

outcome_analysis: Localyze moved from an employee relocation idea to an employer-paid immigration and mobility platform, raised a $12M Series A in July 2021 and a $35M Series B in September 2022, and grew to roughly 100 people. Boundless announced its acquisition on October 1, 2025 for an undisclosed price, which fits sector consolidation, though the lack of a later round suggests growth was slower than the Series B implied.
notes: No competitor source dated near the 2019 batch was found, so the list is empty. TechCrunch 2022 names Bridge US, LegalPad, Jobbatical and relocation agencies, recorded here only as later context. The 2020 seed of $2.1M comes from one secondary article (Startup City Hamburg) and aggregators list about $1.3M in 2019; treat the seed size as uncertain. Series B valuation not disclosed; TechCrunch said a nine-figure sum. Totals of $47M to $48M reported by aggregators.
